scope.flow: checkPoolAndGetCenterPrice oracle price validation and fallback to spot price
scope.environment: on-chain Uniswap V3 style pool oracle consumed by downstream contracts such as LiquidityManager

statements.text: oldestTimestamp + SECONDS_AGO < block.timestamp, so the TWAP observation window has expired
The oracle query fails, i.e. success is false
The slot0 spot price is manipulated
A downstream contract calls checkPoolAndGetCenterPrice to obtain a validated center price
checkPoolAndGetCenterPrice returns centerSqrtPriceX96 (spot price) directly instead of reverting, bypassing all deviation checks when the TWAP window is expired or the oracle query fails
When the TWAP window is expired or the oracle query fails, checkPoolAndGetCenterPrice must not return the spot price as a validated center price; it should revert rather than bypass deviation checks
The center price returned to downstream contracts must have passed the deviation checks against the TWAP rather than being the raw spot price
The protocol's safety reliance on `checkPoolAndGetCenterPrice` creates a false sense of security.
providing any downstream contract (like `LiquidityManager`) with a poisoned baseline

ambiguities: Report does not state who triggers the expired TWAP window or failed oracle query, nor whether an attacker can cause these conditions.
Report does not specify the concrete downstream operation or value at risk in LiquidityManager.
No explicit numeric deviation bound or expected-versus-actual values are given beyond the formulas.
Bypassing all deviation checks is stated as a mechanism/condition rather than a distinct harmful outcome.
